audit.whatIsWrong: The reflect is on the wrong ability everywhere on this page. Ten fields call it 'her R reflect' or 'her reflect'. Rebuttal is Mel's W: it forms a barrier that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage, and grants move speed. Her R, Golden Eclipse, is a global strike on Overwhelm-marked enemies at 25000 range and reflects nothing.
audit.why: This is the single most consequential fact in the matchup and the page had it on the wrong button and the wrong timer. A player tracking a 120/100/80 ultimate to decide when to commit is tracking the wrong cooldown — Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s at 250 range, which is the actual punishable window and a far longer one. Worse, the specific danger is unstated: Explosive Cask carries the projectile flag, so it is the ability Rebuttal reflects, while Body Slam is a charge and Barrel Roll is a rolled cask. Rebuttal also prevents damage outright for its duration, so even a non-projectile combo dumped into it is simply wasted. And Golden Eclipse being global means her ult reaches you after you disengage, which no field mentioned.
audit.corrected: Every reflect reference re-attributed to Rebuttal (W) with its 26-38s cooldown, the projectile-vs-Cask specific stated, and Golden Eclipse's global reach written into the late text.
sources: brief enemyKit W text and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: Labelled TRICKY at 7.5/10 with an orange tone on a 57.1% Emerald+ win rate over 338 games — the strongest lane in this slice was presented as a hard one. Three chart rows also disagreed with the whys printed under them.
audit.why: 57.1% is a clearly favoured lane and the mechanics support it: Mel has no dash and no escape from a landed Body Slam, and the page's own whys say so. whys[1] says Q+W 'out-sustains her ranged poke for free' while win[1] said Skill; whys[2] says outright 'this window is hers' while win[2] said Gragas; whys[4] calls level 6 'a genuine all-in on an escape-less mage' while win[4] said Mel. Only level 1 (her 950 Q against your one ability) and level 3-5 (long cooldowns plus a live Rebuttal) are not yours.
audit.corrected: diff TRICKY to FAV, diffRating 7.5/10 to 4/10, carryRating 8/10 to 7/10, tone to green, and the chart aligned as one atomic group to Mel / Gragas / Mel / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas with ratings 3-7-4-7-7-7-7.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer phase rows were untouched boilerplate with no numbers, and they named Solar Snare as the matchup-defining cooldown.
audit.why: Solar Snare is a 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s root at 1000 range — real, but it comes back every ten seconds and is not what decides whether your all-in works. Rebuttal at 26-38s is. The spike shape is: level 2 when Drunken Rage plus Happy Hour out-sustain her 950 Q, level 3-5 when her poke is safe and your cooldowns are long, and level 6 onward when a landed Body Slam kills an escape-less mage provided Rebuttal is spent.
audit.corrected: phases[1], [2] and [4] rewritten with the real ranges and the Rebuttal condition; breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt around Rebuttal with Solar Snare demoted to its own line.

notes: Largest correction in this slice: ten fields attributed Mel's reflect to her ultimate. Rebuttal is her W (barrier, prevents damage, reflects projectiles, 38/35/33/29/26s at 250 range); Golden Eclipse is a global 25000-range Overwhelm strike with no reflect. The player-facing consequence is specific and was never stated — Explosive Cask carries the projectile flag and is the ability that gets reflected, while Body Slam (charge) and Barrel Roll (rolled cask) do not. I did not claim Rebuttal blocks pathing despite its derived 'terrain' flag; Riot's text describes a barrier around herself, not created terrain. Mirror mel__gragas.json was already audited and its findings (Happy Hour is the sustain, no 'Q pool'; Body Slam stuns and Cask is the displacement) are consistent with everything written here. Gender slips calling Mel 'he' survive in several inherited full-layer strings I had no other reason to touch — worth a sweep.
